data.body: Windows sweep run 35551741150 root cause follow-up: the filed production copy path is fixed by 290424c8491. `test_copy_rewrites_readonly_linked_worktree_git_pointer` now reaches `assert_store_self_contained(copied)` and fails only because the assertion compares Windows backslash `str(resolve())` against Git's forward-slash `gitdir:` pointer spelling. The 2 remaining `.tickets-tracker/.git` `PermissionError` failures in this file are test-construction only: `test_half_fixed_copy_is_rejected` and `test_bare_worktree_repair_is_destructive_and_is_rejected` manually use `shutil.copytree` plus the module-local `_rewrite`, which opens the copied `.tickets-tracker/.git` marker with `Path.write_text(..., mode='w')` and bypasses the production `_clone_template` / `_write_rewritten_path` safe path. I reproduced the same mechanism on macOS by clearing write bits and seeing direct `write_text` raise `PermissionError`, while the production copy-path subset passes. Minimal local fix changes those broken-shape tests to start from `_clone_template` and then corrupt only non-hidden metadata where needed, and changes separator assertions to compare `Path.resolve().as_posix()`. Full file: `pytest -q tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` passes. `make verify` ran to completion and failed only with the expected 17 macOS-arm64 pypandoc `Bad CPU type` failures (13 wiki_render, 3 rich_text_cutover, 1 diff_comments_cutover_neutral). Out of d724 scope in the same Windows evidence: sibling-origin relocation not repointed on Windows, POSIX mode `0o600` assertion reports `0o666` on Windows, and opcert isolation requires OpenSSH >= 8.9 where the Windows runner lacks ssh-keygen.
